title: Scala: Collections
description: Write a Scala program demonstrating List, Map, Set, and functional operations.

codeTemplate.scala:
object Main extends App {
  // List
  val numbers = List(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
  println(s"Numbers: $numbers")
  println(s"Sum: ${numbers.sum}")
  println(s"Doubled: ${numbers.map(_ * 2)}")
  println(s"Evens: ${numbers.filter(_ % 2 == 0)}")

  // Map
  val scores = Map("Alice" -> 95, "Bob" -> 87, "Charlie" -> 92)
  println(s"\nScores: $scores")
  println(s"Alice: ${scores("Alice")}")

  // Higher-order functions
  val words = List("apple", "banana", "cherry", "date")
  println(s"\nLong words: ${words.filter(_.length > 5)}")
  println(s"Upper: ${words.map(_.toUpperCase)}")
  
  val triple = (n: Int) => n * 3
  println(s"\nTripled: ${numbers.map(triple)}")
}

verificationTest: output.includes('Numbers: List(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)') && output.includes('Sum: 15') && output.includes('Doubled: List(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)') && output.includes('Alice: 95')
hints: Scala collections are immutable by default
`_` is a placeholder syntax for anonymous function parameters
`Map(k -> v)` creates a map with arrow syntax
